status: Reference ranges for beginner solo drills. These project settings are awaiting independent coaching validation.

PROJECT.title: Project rubric and measurement definitions
PROJECT.scope: The ranges, points and timing limits used to score each drill.

directional_cues.lunge.front_knee.above: For this classical drill, rehearse a short lunge, pause at the finish, and compare front-knee flexion and foot placement with your coach's reference. Increase the range only after reviewing the recorded finish.
directional_cues.lunge.front_knee.below: Repeat a shorter-range lunge with a controlled finish and compare its front-leg configuration with your coach's reference. Do not force a deeper bend to pursue a numerical score.
directional_cues.lunge.rear_knee.below: Rehearse en garde, a short lunge, a paused finish, and recovery. Review rear-leg extension at the pause; avoid forcing or locking the knee.
directional_cues.lunge.elbow.below: For this selected classical extension drill, first practise weapon-arm extension with the feet still, then add a short lunge. Compare the measured elbow configuration at the finish. This is not a universal rule for every competitive attack.
directional_cues.lunge.trunk.above: Start in guard, take a short lunge and hold the finish for two seconds. Pause the clip there and compare your torso angle with your coach's reference before lengthening the lunge.
directional_cues.lunge.arm_lead.below: For this classical coordination drill, rehearse a visible arm-extension initiation followed by front-foot movement at a slow, comfortable tempo. Compare the two recorded onset times. This observation does not determine attack priority.
directional_cues.lunge.arm_lead.above: Repeat the extension and short lunge as a continuous coordination drill and compare their separately observed onset times. The timing band is a project setting, not a universal competitive requirement.
directional_cues.step.foot_order.below: Rehearse one slow basic step from a paused guard: front foot initiates an advance, rear foot initiates a retreat. Pause again after the following foot moves, and compare the recorded foot-onset order.
directional_cues.step.stance_error.above: Perform one basic step with a pause before and after. Compare the final ankle spacing with your calibrated guard, and repeat at a shorter range if your coach intends the same guard spacing.
directional_cues.arm_extension.elbow.below: For this arm-only reference drill, keep the feet still, extend the weapon arm comfortably, pause, and return to guard. Compare the recorded elbow angle with your coach-approved reference; do not force the joint.

lunge: Review the observed front-leg configuration against a coach-approved classical lunge reference.
Review rear-leg extension at the indicated frame; avoid forcing or locking the joint.
For this classical straight-extension drill, review arm extension with your coach.
Review the indicated trunk inclination. The classical reference uses a relatively upright torso.
Compare arm and front-foot movement onsets in slow motion for this classical drill. This does not determine priority.
Repeat the same drill at a comfortable tempo and compare the time from the start to the peak.
Review the observed vertical hip excursion; this image measure is not a centre-of-mass or balance measurement.
Compare the indicated knee and ankle positions with a coach. This rule does not diagnose loading or injury risk.
Watch the torso through the lunge. Check when its angle changes and whether that change is part of the drill.
Review repeated reversals of the measured arm reach during extension. This does not measure sword-tip accuracy.
step: Review the final front-knee configuration against your calibrated guard.
Review the final rear-knee configuration against your calibrated guard.
Check whether the feet returned to the intended guard spacing after the step.
Review the indicated final trunk configuration.
In an advance, review front-foot initiation; in a retreat, review rear-foot initiation. This cue is for the selected basic drill.
Compare repetitions of the same drill at the same intended tempo; do not chase a faster score.
Review the observed hip image excursion while maintaining the intended stepping pattern.
Review foot spacing during the marked basic step. No diagnosis of balance is made.
Review trunk consistency across the step.
en_garde: Compare the observed front-leg configuration with your coach's guard reference.
Compare the observed rear-leg configuration with your coach's guard reference.
Review the observed trunk inclination for this guard drill.
Hold the intended guard long enough to obtain a stable observation.
Review unintended foot movement over this static guard interval.
Review the observed vertical hip image excursion during the hold.
Compare trunk consistency over the observed hold.
arm_extension: Review the indicated elbow extension for this straight-extension drill.
Review torso inclination while extending the weapon arm.
Review whether the intended guard spacing was retained.
Compare the observed extension interval across repetitions of the same drill.
For an arm-only drill, review the measured foot displacement.
Review the measured hip excursion during the arm-only drill.
Review changes in the direction of measured arm reach; blade accuracy is unmeasured.
recovery: Compare the observed final front-knee configuration with your guard reference.
Compare the observed final rear-knee configuration with your guard reference.
Review the final distance between the feet after returning to guard.
Review recovery at a controlled, repeatable tempo rather than forcing speed.
Review observed hip excursion during the recovery; this is not a balance test.
Review the final guard hold at the marked end of the recovery.
Watch the torso as you return to guard. Look for the part of the recovery where its angle changes most.
